chunks: With this chain of transmission, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said:

Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is an angel among the angels whose upper half is fire and whose lower half is ice; neither does the fire melt the ice, nor does the ice extinguish the fire. He stands calling with a high-pitched voice: 'Glory be to Allah, who withheld the heat of this fire so that it does not melt this ice, and withheld the cold of this ice so that it does not extinguish the heat of this fire. O Allah, O Combiner of the ice and fire, unite the hearts of Your believing servants in Your obedience.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the angel with half fire and half ice in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this unique cosmological imagery to illustrate Allah’s power over contradictory elements, serving as a metaphor for divine unity (tawhid) and the potential for harmony among believers. The angel’s continuous praise highlights the perfection of Allah’s attribute as the Unifier (al-Mu'allif), linking the physical miracle of coexisting fire and ice to the spiritual goal of unifying the hearts of the faithful in obedience.
